items.title: A New Topic Opens: Defilement Establishment, and Its Three Kinds

items.zh: 復次，云何雜染施設建立？謂由三種雜染應知。何等為三？一、煩惱雜染，二、業雜染，三、生雜染。
items.en: Further, how is defilement establishment to be understood? It should be understood through three kinds of defilement. What are the three? First, afflictive defilement; second, karmic defilement; third, rebirth defilement.

items.title: Affliction's Nine-Part Outline, and Its Basic Nature: Restlessness Itself

items.zh: 煩惱雜染云何？嗢拕南曰：自性、若分別、因、位、及與門、上品、顛倒攝、差別、諸過患。當知煩惱雜染，由自性故，分別故，因故，位故，門故，上品故，顛倒攝故，差別故，過患故。解釋應知。
items.en: What is afflictive defilement? A summary verse states: nature, and classification, cause and stage, and gateway, superior grade, what is subsumed under distortion, differences, and faults. It should be understood that afflictive defilement is to be explained through nature, through classification, through cause, through stage, through gateway, through superior grade, through what is subsumed under distortion, through differences, and through faults.

items.zh: 煩惱自性者，謂若法生時，其相自然不寂靜起；由彼起故，不寂靜行相續而轉，是名略說煩惱自性。
items.en: As for affliction's own nature: whenever such a phenomenon arises, its characteristic is to arise, of its own accord, as a state of restlessness — and because it has thus arisen, a continuous current of restless activity carries on from it. This, stated briefly, is affliction's own nature.

items.title: Classifying Affliction: One Root, Two Paths of Abandonment, Three Realms, Four Moral Grades

items.zh: 煩惱分別者，或立一種。謂由煩惱雜染義故。或分二種。謂見道所斷、修道所斷。或分三種。謂欲繫、色繫、無色繫。
items.en: As for the classification of affliction: it may be posited as a single kind, in the sense that all affliction alike constitutes defilement. It may be divided into two kinds: what is abandoned through the path of seeing, and what is abandoned through the path of cultivation. It may be divided into three kinds: what is bound to the desire realm, what is bound to the form realm, and what is bound to the formless realm.

items.zh: 或分四種。謂欲繫記無記、色繫無記、無色繫無記。
items.en: It may be divided into four kinds: what is bound to the desire realm and morally determinate, what is bound to the desire realm and morally indeterminate, what is bound to the form realm and morally indeterminate, and what is bound to the formless realm and morally indeterminate.

items.title: Five Truths Misunderstood, Six Basic Kinds, Seven Latent Tendencies, Eight With the Two Graspings

items.zh: 或分五種。謂見苦所斷、見集所斷、見滅所斷、見道所斷、修道所斷。或分六種。謂貪、恚、慢、無明、見、疑。
items.en: It may be divided into five kinds: what is abandoned by seeing suffering, what is abandoned by seeing its origin, what is abandoned by seeing its cessation, what is abandoned by seeing the path, and what is abandoned through cultivation. It may be divided into six kinds: craving, hatred, conceit, ignorance, view, and doubt.

items.zh: 或分七種。謂七種隨眠：一、欲貪隨眠，二、瞋恚隨眠，三、有貪隨眠，四、慢隨眠，五、無明隨眠，六、見隨眠，七、疑隨眠。或分八種。謂貪、恚、慢、無明、疑、見，及二種取。
items.en: It may be divided into seven kinds — seven latent tendencies: craving for desire, hatred, craving for existence, conceit, ignorance, view, and doubt. It may be divided into eight kinds: craving, hatred, conceit, ignorance, doubt, view, and the two kinds of grasping.

items.title: Nine Fetters That Bind Beings to Suffering, and the Ten Fundamental Afflictions

items.zh: 或分九種。謂九結，一、愛結，二、恚結，三、慢結，四、無明結，五、見結，六、取結，七、疑結，八、嫉結，九、慳結。
items.en: It may be divided into nine kinds — nine fetters: the fetter of craving, the fetter of hatred, the fetter of conceit, the fetter of ignorance, the fetter of view, the fetter of grasping, the fetter of doubt, the fetter of envy, and the fetter of stinginess.

items.zh: 或分十種。一、薩迦耶見，二、邊執見，三、邪見，四、見取，五、戒禁取，六、貪，七、恚，八、慢，九、無明，十、疑。
items.en: It may be divided into ten kinds: self-view, extreme views, wrong view, view-grasping, precept-and-vow grasping, craving, hatred, conceit, ignorance, and doubt.

items.title: The Full Tally: One Hundred and Twenty-Eight Kinds of Affliction

items.zh: 或分一百二十八煩惱。謂即上十煩惱，由迷執十二種諦建立應知。何等名為十二種諦？謂欲界苦諦、集諦，色界苦諦、集諦，無色界苦諦、集諦。欲界增上彼遍智果，彼遍智所顯滅諦、道諦；色界增上彼遍智果，彼遍智所顯滅諦、道諦；無色界增上彼遍智果，彼遍智所顯滅諦、道諦。
items.en: It may be divided into one hundred twenty-eight afflictions: the ten afflictions just given, established through confusion regarding twelve specific truths, as should be understood. What are these twelve truths? The desire realm's truth of suffering and truth of origin; the form realm's truth of suffering and truth of origin; the formless realm's truth of suffering and truth of origin; the desire realm's truth of cessation and truth of the path, manifested as the result and the very activity of complete understanding; the form realm's truth of cessation and truth of the path, likewise manifested; and the formless realm's truth of cessation and truth of the path, likewise manifested.

items.zh: 此中於欲界苦、集諦、及於欲界增上滅、道諦、具有十煩惱迷執。於色界苦、集諦，及於彼增上滅、道諦，除瞋，有餘煩惱迷執。如於色界，於無色界亦爾。於欲界對治修中，有六煩惱迷執。謂除邪見、見取、戒禁取、疑。
items.en: Here, with respect to the desire realm's truths of suffering and origin, and its truths of cessation and the path, all ten afflictions arise in confusion. With respect to the form realm's truths of suffering and origin, and its truths of cessation and the path, all afflictions but hatred arise in confusion. As with the form realm, so too with the formless realm. Within the desire realm's cultivation of the antidote, six afflictions arise in confusion — namely, all but wrong view, view-grasping, precept-grasping, and doubt.

items.zh: 於色界對治修中，有五煩惱迷執。謂於上六中除瞋。如於色界對治修中，於無色對治修中亦爾。如迷執，障礙亦爾。

items.title: The Root of All Views: Self-View, and Its Twenty Forms

items.zh: 薩迦耶見者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故；及由任運失念故，等隨觀執五種取蘊，若分別、不分別染污慧為體。
items.en: As for self-view: it arises through keeping company with unwholesome persons, hearing false teachings, and unsound reasoning attention, as well as through a spontaneous lapse of mindfulness — and consists in observing and grasping, wholly or partially, the five aggregates of clinging as a self, taking as its own nature a defiled discernment, whether deliberately reasoned or unreflectively spontaneous.

items.title: Extreme Views (Eternalism and Annihilationism), and Wrong View That Denies Cause and Effect

items.zh: 邊執見者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，及由任運失念故，執五取蘊為我性已，等隨觀執為斷為常，若分別、若不分別染污慧為體。
items.en: As for extreme views: having, through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, unsound attention, or a spontaneous lapse of mindfulness, already grasped the five aggregates of clinging as a self's own nature, one goes on to observe and grasp that self, wholly or partially, as either annihilated or permanent — again a defiled discernment, whether deliberately reasoned or spontaneous, as its own nature.

items.zh: 邪見者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，撥因撥果，或撥作用，壞真實事，唯用分別染污慧為體。
items.en: As for wrong view: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, and unsound attention, and consists in denying cause, denying effect, or denying causal function, and undermining what is genuinely real — a defiled discernment that is always deliberately reasoned, never spontaneous, as its own nature.

items.title: View-Grasping: Insisting One's Own Mistaken View Is Supreme

items.zh: 見取者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，以薩迦耶見、邊執見、邪見，及所依、所緣、所因俱有相應等法，比方他見，等隨觀執為最、為上、勝妙、第一，唯用分別染污慧為體。
items.en: As for view-grasping: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, and unsound attention, and consists in comparing self-view, extreme views, and wrong view — together with their supporting faculties, objects, and seeds, and all that co-arises and operates alongside them — against the views of others, and then observing and grasping one's own, wholly or partially, as the finest, the highest, the most sublime, the very first — a defiled discernment that is always deliberately reasoned, as its own nature.

items.title: Precept-and-Vow Grasping: Mistaking a Ritual Observance for the Path Itself

items.zh: 戒禁取者，謂由親近不善丈夫、聞非正法、不如理作意故，即於彼見、彼見隨行若戒若禁，及所依、所緣、所因俱有相應等法，等隨觀執為清淨、為解脫、為出離，唯用分別染污慧為體。
items.en: As for precept-and-vow grasping: it arises through keeping bad company, hearing false teachings, and unsound attention, and consists in taking the precepts (bodily and verbal restraints) or the vows (prescribed dress, diet, and deportment) that follow from those very mistaken views — together with their supporting faculties, objects, seeds, and all that co-arises with them — and observing and grasping them, wholly or partially, as themselves constituting purity, liberation, or genuine release, a defiled discernment that is always deliberately reasoned, as its own nature.

blocks.text: Fascicle 8 reaches the fifth and last gateway of the three grounds of thought: **defilement** (雜染), in three kinds: afflictive defilement (煩惱雜染), karmic defilement (業雜染), and rebirth defilement (生雜染). Venerable Miào Jìng: these three are the first two noble truths, suffering and its origin. This fascicle covers the first two kinds and is, in effect, a manual of Buddhist psychology of the afflictions and of karma. Today: what affliction is, how it is classified, and the five kinds of wrong view.

Affliction is explained under nine headings. Its nature: "Whenever such a phenomenon arises, its characteristic is to arise, of its own accord, as a state of **restlessness** (不寂靜), and because it has thus arisen, a continuous current of restless activity follows." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pīxún jì*: "affliction is another name for restlessness." This is the most practical definition one could ask for: whenever the mind is unquiet, look for an affliction.

Affliction can be divided many ways: as abandoned by the path of seeing or the path of cultivation (Venerable Miào Jìng: one who has seen the path will never again fall to the lower realms); as bound to each of the three realms; and as the six root afflictions, the seven **latent tendencies** (隨眠, Day 7). Master Cháng Bǎi's image for a latent tendency: "like a person asleep: no activity; on waking, immediately active." The seven split craving into craving for sense desire and craving for existence (attachment to the form and formless absorptions).

The nine **fetters** (結): craving, hatred, conceit, ignorance, view, grasping, doubt, envy, and stinginess. Master Cháng Bǎi: envy is listed especially for monastics, who may envy another's wisdom; stinginess especially for lay people.
The ten fundamental afflictions are the "five dull" (craving, hatred, conceit, ignorance, doubt) and the "five sharp", the five views below.

Counted by realm and by which of the four truths they obscure, the afflictions number 112 abandoned by seeing, plus 16 abandoned by cultivation: 128. Venerable Miào Jìng walks through the arithmetic; the upper realms lack hatred, so they have fewer. The point of such counting is that the path is precise: particular insights remove particular afflictions.

The root of all views is **self-view** (薩迦耶見, *satkāya-dṛṣṭi*), "view of the perishing aggregates as self". It arises from bad company, false teaching, unsound attention, and spontaneous lapses of mindfulness. It has twenty forms: for each aggregate, four ways of relating it to a self (form is self; self has form; form belongs to self; self is in form). Venerable Miào Jìng: conceptual self-grasping ends at stream-entry; innate self-grasping only at arhatship (Day 22).

**Extreme views** (邊執見): having taken the aggregates as a self, grasping that self as permanent or as annihilated (Days 44–49). **Wrong view** (邪見): denying cause and effect, denying the functioning of karma, undermining what is real. Venerable Miào Jìng: there is no innate wrong view, only the deliberately reasoned kind; nobody is born denying karma.

**View-grasping** (見取) takes one's own views as supreme. Master Cháng Bǎi's practical warning: "Meditating without studying the Dharma is dangerous; you may fall into view-grasping, taking the absorbed state for nirvāṇa." **Precept-and-vow grasping** (戒禁取) takes the observances that follow from such views as purity and liberation, like the dog vow of Day 51. Venerable Miào Jìng counts the rituals of every other religion here; a Buddhist reader may add that Buddhist rituals done in the same spirit fall here too.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through which three kinds of defilement is defilement establishment understood?
quiz.why: "First, afflictive defilement; second, karmic defilement; third, rebirth defilement." This is the last of the five gateways on the three grounds. Fascicle 8 completes affliction and gets partway through karma. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pixunji*: all contaminated dharmas are called defiled; the contaminant is affliction, which defiles.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the nature of affliction?
options: when it arises, its mark is to arise of itself as restlessness, and restless activity continues from it
quiz.why: "Whenever such a phenomenon arises, its characteristic is to arise, of its own accord, as a state of restlessness — and because it has thus arisen, a continuous current of restless activity carries on from it." Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction is restless itself and unsettles others too; the *Abhidharmasamuccaya* lists distraction, distortion, agitation, torpor, heedlessness, shamelessness.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, if affliction is divided into two, what are they?
options: abandoned by the path of seeing and by the path of cultivation
quiz.why: "It may be divided into two kinds: what is abandoned through the path of seeing, and what is abandoned through the path of cultivation." Three: bound to the desire, form, or formless realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing cuts the 112 conceptually arisen afflictions; cultivation cuts the spontaneous ones.

quiz.q: What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for "latent tendency" (隨眠)?
options: like a sleeping person — inactive, but active the moment they wake
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Like a person asleep — no activity; on waking, immediately active." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Asleep you don't move; awake you get to work. Afflictions are like that." Hence "sleep."

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT among the treatise's nine fetters?
quiz.why: The nine: craving, hatred, conceit, ignorance, view, grasping, doubt, envy, stinginess. Remorse is not one (it is among the eight wrappings). Venerable Miào Jìng: a fetter "joins you with suffering."

quiz.q: Self-view has "twenty forms." How are they counted, and when are conceptual and innate self-grasping each cut?
options: four for each aggregate (form is self, self has form, form belongs to self, self is in form) — twenty; conceptual grasping ends at stream-entry, innate at arhatship
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Taking form as an example: form is self, self has form, form belongs to self, self is in form." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Five aggregates, four each — twenty"; "conceptual self-grasping is cut at stream-entry; the spontaneous, innate kind remains until arhatship."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is view-grasping?
options: comparing self-view, extreme views, and wrong view (with their bases and objects) against others' views, and grasping one's own as finest, highest, most sublime, first
quiz.why: "Comparing self-view, extreme views, and wrong view — together with their supporting faculties, objects, and seeds … — against the views of others, and then … grasping one's own … as the finest, the highest, the most sublime, the very first." Venerable Miào Jìng: supports are the six faculties, objects the six sense-fields; it amounts to "taking non-cessation for cessation, non-path for path."
